title: Functoriality of unit restriction along an arbitrary étale lift
statement: Let $X,Z,W$ be schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $p:Z\to X$, $q:W\to Z$, and $g:W\to X$ with $g=p\circ q$. Fix a commutative ring $\Lambda$, a sheaf $F$ of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], an étale object $U\to X$, and a lift $v:Z\to U$ over $X$. Define $\delta_v:Z\to U\times_X Z$ by $(v,1_Z)$ using the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]. Define $r(p,F,U,v):F(U)\to\Gamma(Z,p^{-1}F)$ by the inverse-image adjunction unit [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] at $U$, restriction along $\delta_v$, and inverse terminal evaluation. Then $r(p,F,U,v)$ followed by the global inverse-image map along $q$ and the canonical composition identification $q^{-1}p^{-1}F\cong g^{-1}F$ equals $r(g,F,U,v\circ q)$. Here the global inverse-image map is the same unit construction as [def-weil-pbc-finite-section-pullback], for arbitrary $q$. There are no qcqs, properness, geometric-point, or invertibility assumptions.

proof.text: Express the global inverse-image map via the unit evaluated at the identity étale object and its terminal lift. Terminal uniqueness and naturality of terminal evaluation prove this formula from the definition.

Move the first graph restriction through the second adjunction unit by naturality. The canonical composition comparison is the isomorphism of left adjoints compatible with the composed units; its unit equation (upperStarComp_hom_app_unit_app in the adopted source Coherence module) gives the displayed composite-unit equation, after cancelling its inverse. Evaluate at U and move the comparison through the restriction by naturality. This is a formal consequence of the adjunction definition, not any strict-local comparison theorem.

The remaining composite of the terminal lift, the pullback of the graph, and the iterated-fibre-product comparison has first projection q followed by v and second projection the identity. Pullback extensionality identifies it with the graph for q followed by v. Cancel terminal evaluation and its inverse. The same equations include empty schemes and the zero coefficient ring.
